Protected-path enforcement is double-belted. (1) scripts/fleet/verify-protected.mjs walks the diff against policy.json's protected_paths and fails on any hit that lacks the bootstrap exemption (feature/fleet-p-1-* while policy.json is absent at the base), the own-phase-receipt exemption, the fleet-ledger-rows exemption, or the orchestrator_protected_change trailer (Fleet-Role: orchestrator + Protected-Change: <reason>). (2) .github/workflows/protected-paths.yml fails any PR that touches a protected path without the human-required label, with the same exemption table. The merge-phase.mjs 8-gate sequence (halt, pr-readable, head-matches, base-main, branch-pattern, receipt, checks, review, attest) ensures PRs that bypass CI cannot land. The two surfaces I verified empirically: (a) selftest's guard-control line proves the rule is what produces the deny (a policy with protected_paths:[] lets the planted write through, then re-adding the rule denies it), and (b) the M2 mutant (removing scripts/fleet/** from policy.json) was caught by selftest's planted check before the wrapper could be re-shipped. The blast radius of any single builder unit is therefore one unprotected file at a time, and the protected set is the union of the two lists above plus the wrapper itself.

All outbound actions are enumerated in scripts/fleet/policy.json's roles table and denied by default. (1) orchestrator: may read, spawn, integrate, run-gate, review, push, open-pr, merge-via-merge-phase; may_not: edit-product-source-outside-bootstrap, --no-verify, force-push, direct gh pr merge. The guard.mjs special-case for `\bgh pr merge\b` (releaser+via:merge-phase only, before the forbidden_commands loop) is the single sanctioned merge path. (2) releaser: may release-gate, push-feature-fleet-branch, open-one-pr, merge-via-merge-phase; may_not: direct gh pr merge, force-push, --no-verify, override-variable. (3) builder: may edit-in-own-sandbox, npm-scripts, tests; may_not: install, git push, gh, protected-paths, secrets, network-beyond-registry. (4) reader: may read-repo, read-web-allowlist, return-json; may_not: write, shell-mutation, spend, publish. (5) verifier: may read, run-dod-fresh-context, return-receipt-json; may_not: edit-source, edit-contracts, write-receipts-dir. (6) judge: may read-case-and-output, return-schema-verdict; may_not: tools, see-generator-identity. (7) scheduler: may cloudroom-automation-start, read-ledgers; may_not: edit, write-connector, spend-outside-wrapper. The forbidden_commands list (16 entries) covers force-push, --no-verify, gh pr merge, git reset --hard, git branch -D, prisma migrate deploy, prisma db push, vercel --prod, vercel deploy, npm/pnpm/yarn install/add (the builder install deny), rm -rf /, and curl -X POST. denied_mcp_tool_classes covers deploy, promote, apply_migration, execute_sql, merge_branch, reset_branch, create_or_update_file, send_message, publish, post. The selftest planted list exercises the cross-section: a builder running `gh pr merge 1 --squash` is denied; a releaser running `gh pr merge 1 --squash` without via:merge-phase is denied; a releaser running `gh pr merge 1 --squash` with via:merge-phase is allowed.
